A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 6DOPE-GS work, and all supplied pages are readable. v1 includes supplementary Sections 6–10 and detailed result tables; v2 ends after the references despite retaining an appendix pointer. These documented omissions can be compared without inferring changes to the underlying implementation.

before.justification: v1 reports original pose-tracking, reconstruction, runtime and ablation results on HO3D and YCBInEOAT, plus a live-camera demonstration and detailed supplementary results.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark and live-camera results and reports additional MonoGS comparisons and representation ablations in Tables 1–3.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.5 retain the same initialization, joint 2D Gaussian/pose optimization, dynamic keyframe selection, opacity pruning and pose-graph pipeline. The new 3DGS configuration is an ablation, not a replacement of the proposed method. Missing supplementary specifications do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate HO3D, YCBInEOAT and live RGB-D object tracking. Dataset descriptions and coverage remain unchanged. v2 Section 4.6 reproduces the real-time experiment from v1 supplementary Section 10; extending ablations to YCBInEOAT adds no new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: MonoGS(RGB-D) is newly evaluated on both datasets and included in Figure 4. Conversely, the YCBInEOAT comparisons with BundleSDF-async and BundleSDF-lite in v1 Table 5 are absent from v2, although both variants remain in the HO3D comparison. Separate published and reproduced BundleTrack/BundleSDF rows are consolidated.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce a 3DGS replacement control and specify RGB-D input for MonoGS. Retained dataset splits, pose/reconstruction metrics and timing hardware remain unchanged. Average time per frame was already evaluated in v1; its appearance in the main tables is not a new metric.

E4.justification: Table 3 expands keyframe-selection and pruning ablations from HO3D to both datasets and adds a direct 2DGS-versus-3DGS test on each. This substantially broadens component validation. However, v1's qualitative pitcher-handle ablation and supplementary symmetry-related failure case are absent from v2.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The retained median-absolute-deviation calculation is an algorithmic outlier filter, not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds MonoGS and expanded ablation results but omits detailed Tables 4–5. HO3D Table 3 Chamfer distances for no-keyframe-selection/no-pruning/final change from 0.41/0.42/0.43 to 0.42/0.44/0.41 cm, reversing the reconstruction ranking; v1's appendix separately reported a conflicting 0.37 cm final mean. v2's YCBInEOAT distances of 0.15 cm for 6DOPE-GS and 0.53 cm for BundleSDF already appeared in v1 Table 5, so these are not established new gains. Main pose scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v1 supplementary Section 6 explicitly defines the masked color, Huber-depth, depth-distortion and normal losses and the joint Gaussian/SE(3) optimization objective. These mathematical specifications, particularly Equations 3–7, are absent from v2. Main-text rendering mathematics remains unchanged; this is lost formal specification, not evidence of a changed objective.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims: model-free joint pose tracking and reconstruction using 2DGS, dynamic keyframe selection, opacity-based pruning, competitive accuracy, approximately fivefold speedup and live tracking at 3.5 Hz. Added comparisons support rather than redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 revises the HO3D accuracy explanation toward occlusion-reduced supervision and minibatch SDF optimization, and adds explanations for MonoGS and 3DGS-ablation weaknesses. The broad conclusion limitations remain, but v1's specific discussion of symmetry, large rotational corrections and pitcher-handle failures is no longer included.

D1.justification: v2 omits substantial reproducibility information from supplementary Sections 7–8: mesh-extraction settings, mask sources, initialization, loss weights, optimization schedules, anchor counts and pruning thresholds. It also removes the first-frame ground-truth evaluation disclosure from Section 4.2. Existing live-camera details are relocated, while the added MonoGS repository pointer and unspecified 'optimized parameters' provide limited replacement detail.

R1.justification: v2 adds the IRGS citation and discusses empirical differences from the already-cited Gaussian Splatting SLAM/MonoGS work. XMem, Open3D and Yugay et al.'s Gaussian-SLAM references disappear with supplementary material. The central positioning relative to BundleSDF and Gaussian-Splatting SLAM remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Rewriting concentrates on introductory motivation, baseline descriptions, result interpretation and the conclusion; the abstract and method narrative remain substantially identical. The real-time section moves from supplementary Section 10 into Section 4.6, while the remaining supplementary sections are omitted. The main organizational sequence is retained.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 gain runtime columns and revised row structures, and Table 3 becomes a two-dataset ablation table. Figure 3 replaces reconstruction panels; Figure 4 is redrawn with side-by-side plots, altered axes and legends. v1 Figure 7 becomes v2 Figure 5, while the pitcher ablation, failure illustration, additional qualitative montage and detailed supplementary tables disappear.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful MonoGS and representation comparisons and makes YCB reconstruction summaries consistent with values already in v1's appendix. However, it loses the explicit joint objective, essential implementation settings, detailed results and concrete failure analysis while still pointing to an absent appendix. These losses reduce reproducibility and auditability enough to outweigh the focused empirical and presentation improvements.
